content: 1. Drospirenone and potassium acid phosphate both elevate serum potassium levels. It is advised to avoid this combination or consider alternative medications due to the risk of hyperkalemia. 2. Drospirenone and potassium chloride both increase serum potassium levels. Avoid or use alternative drugs to mitigate the risk of hyperkalemia. 3. Drospirenone and potassium citrate both elevate serum potassium levels. Avoid or use alternative medications to prevent potential complications. 4. Drospirenone and potassium citrate/citric acid both increase serum potassium levels. Close monitoring is recommended, and caution should be exercised. 5. Potassium iodide and drospirenone both elevate serum potassium levels. Use caution and monitor closely to avoid hyperkalemia. 6. Drospirenone and intravenous potassium phosphates both increase serum potassium levels. Avoid or use alternative drugs to reduce the risk of hyperkalemia. 7. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of praziquantel by altering hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown but considered minor. 8. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of primaquine by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is minor, with unknown clinical significance. 9. Primidone decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs, as this may reduce the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 10. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of progesterone intravaginal gel by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is minor, with unknown clinical significance. 11. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of micronized progesterone by altering hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is minor, with unknown clinical significance. 12. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of natural progesterone by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is minor, with unknown clinical significance. 13. Propranolol and drospirenone both elevate serum potassium levels. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended to avoid hyperkalemia. 14. Ethinylestradiol may increase the serum concentrations of tricyclic antidepressants (TCAs) by reducing oxidative metabolism. This could lead to increased antidepressant serum levels and a higher risk of adverse effects. 15. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of quazepam by altering hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is minor, with unknown clinical significance. 16. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of quetiapine by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is minor, with unknown clinical significance. 17. Quinapril and drospirenone may synergistically increase the risk of hyperkalemia. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of quinidine by altering hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Quinidine may also increase the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 19. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of quinine by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is minor, with unknown clinical significance. 20. Quinupristin/dalfopristin may increase the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of rabeprazole by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is minor, with unknown clinical significance. 22. Ethinylestradiol may increase the levels or effects of ramelteon by altering hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. Close monitoring is recommended. 23. Ramipril and drospirenone may synergistically increase the risk of hyperkalemia. Use caution and monitor closely. 24. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of ranolazine by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Ethinylestradiol may also increase the levels or effects of ranolazine via the same mechanism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 25. Ethinylestradiol may increase the levels or effects of rasagiline by altering hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of regorafenib by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is minor, with unknown clinical significance. 27. Reishi may enhance the effects of drospirenone through pharmacodynamic synergism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown but considered minor. 28. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of repaglinide by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is minor, with unknown clinical significance. 29. Repotrectinib decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol and drospirenone by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs, as this may reduce the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 30. Ribociclib may increase the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Drospirenone may also increase the levels or effects of ribociclib via the same mechanism. These interactions are minor, with unknown clinical significance. 31. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of rifabutin by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Rifabutin decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol via the same mechanism. Avoid or use alternative drugs, as this may reduce the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 32. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs, as this may reduce the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 33. Rifapentine decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs, as this may reduce the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 34. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of rimegepant by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is minor, with unknown clinical significance. 35. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of riociguat by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is minor, with unknown clinical significance. 36. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of ritonavir by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Ritonavir may also increase the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol via the same mechanism. Avoid or use alternative drugs, as significant changes in estrogen plasma levels may occur, potentially reducing the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 37. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of rivaroxaban by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is minor, with unknown clinical significance. 38. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of roflumilast by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is minor, with unknown clinical significance. 39. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of rolapitant by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is minor, with unknown clinical significance. 40. Romidepsin decreases the effects of ethinylestradiol through receptor binding competition. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of romidepsin by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. These interactions are minor, with unknown clinical significance. 41. Ethinylestradiol may increase the levels or effects of ropinirole by altering hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 42. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of ropivacaine by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is minor, with unknown clinical significance. 43. Rosuvastatin may increase the levels of ethinylestradiol through an unspecified interaction mechanism. This interaction is minor, with unknown clinical significance. 44. Rucaparib may increase the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Adjust the dosage of CYP3A4 substrates if clinically indicated. 45. Rufinamide decreases the effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Rufinamide is a weak inducer of CYP3A4 and may decrease the exposure of drugs metabolized by this enzyme. 46. Ethinylestradiol and drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of ruxolitinib (including topical formulations) by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. These interactions are minor, with unknown clinical significance. 47. Sacubitril/valsartan and drospirenone both elevate serum potassium levels. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended to avoid hyperkalemia. 48. Drospirenone and salicylates (non-ASA) both increase serum potassium levels. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 49. Drospirenone increases serum potassium levels, while salmeterol decreases it. The effect of this interaction is unclear; use caution. Drospirenone may also increase the levels or effects of salmeterol by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is minor, with unknown clinical significance. 50. Drospirenone and salsalate both elevate serum potassium levels. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 51. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of saxagliptin by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is minor, with unknown clinical significance. 52. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels of selegiline (oral and transdermal) by inhibiting its N-demethylation. Use caution and monitor closely. 53. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of selpercatinib by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is minor, with unknown clinical significance. 54. Shepherd’s purse may theoretically interfere with blood pressure control when used with drospirenone. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown but considered minor. 55. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of sildenafil by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is minor, with unknown clinical significance. 56. Siltuximab may restore CYP450 enzymatic activity by inhibiting IL-6, potentially affecting the metabolism of CYP substrates with a narrow therapeutic index. Use caution and monitor closely when coadministered with drospirenone or ethinylestradiol. 57. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of simvastatin by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is minor, with unknown clinical significance. 58. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of siponimod by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is minor, with unknown clinical significance. 59. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of sirolimus by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is minor, with unknown clinical significance. 60. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is minor, with unknown clinical significance. 61. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of solifenacin by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is minor, with unknown clinical significance. 62. Ethinylestradiol decreases the levels or effects of somapacitan, somatrogon, and somatropin by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Oral estrogens may reduce serum IGF-1 response to growth hormone analogs, potentially requiring higher GH doses. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 63. Drospirenone may decrease the levels or effects of somapacitan, somatrogon, and somatropin by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 64. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of sonidegib by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is minor, with unknown clinical significance. 65. Drospirenone may increase the levels or effects of sorafenib by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is minor, with unknown clinical significance.
